style.text: Considérons $A, B \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ où $B$ est unitaire. On définit la suite de polynômes $(F_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ par $F_0 = A$ et $F_{k} = A + kB$. Si l'on sait que pour chaque entier naturel $k$, il existe un entier $x_k$ tel que $F_k(x_k) = 0$, prouver que soit $A$ et $B$ partagent un zéro dans $\mathbb{Z}$, soit $A = (aX+b)B$ pour certains entiers $a, b$ avec $a \neq 0$.

exact.text: Démontrer qu'il existe une infinité d'entiers naturels $n$ tels que la décomposition $n^2 = \sum_{k=0}^m a_k 4^k$ vérifie $a_k \in \{1, 2\}$ pour tout $0 \le k \le m$.

paraphrase.text: Prove that the set $S = \{ x \in \mathbb{Z} : x^2 = \sum_{i=0}^k a_i 4^i, a_i \in \{1, 2\} \}$ is infinite.

style.text: Soit $S$ l'ensemble des entiers naturels dont le développement en base 4 n'utilise que les chiffres du sous-ensemble $\{1, 2\}$. Prouver que l'intersection de $S$ avec l'ensemble des carrés parfaits est infinie.

exact.text: Soit $M$ une matrice de taille $n \times n$ dont tous les coefficients valent initialement $k=99$. Deux joueurs, $P_1$ et $P_2$, soustraient alternativement $1$ à tous les éléments d'une ligne ou d'une colonne de leur choix, à condition que tous les éléments de la ligne ou colonne choisie soient strictement positifs avant l'opération. Si $P_1$ commence, pour quelles valeurs de $n$ le second joueur possède-t-il une stratégie gagnante ?

paraphrase.text: Let $G$ be a grid of size $N \times N$ where each cell $(i, j)$ initially contains $K = 99$ tokens. Two players, Alpha and Beta, play a game where a move consists of selecting an index $k \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ and a direction $d \in \{\text{horizontal, vertical}\}$. If $d$ is horizontal, one token is removed from every cell $(k, j)$ for $1 \le j \le N$; if $d$ is vertical, one token is removed from every cell $(i, k)$ for $1 \le i \le N$. A move is legal if and only if every cell in the targeted line currently contains at least one token. Using normal play convention, identify all $N$ such that the second player has a winning strategy.

style.text: Un tableau $n \times n$ contient initialement l'entier $k=99$ dans chaque cellule. Deux joueurs, $P_1$ et $P_2$, jouent alternativement. À chaque tour, un joueur choisit un vecteur ligne ou un vecteur colonne dont toutes les composantes sont strictement positives et retranche $1$ à chaque élément de ce vecteur. Le dernier joueur à pouvoir effectuer un coup gagne. Pour quelles valeurs de $n$ le second joueur possède-t-il une stratégie gagnante ?

exact.text: Soit $\mathbb{P}$ l'ensemble des nombres premiers. Résoudre dans $\mathbb{Z}^+ \times \mathbb{P}$ l'équation $n^k - n = p$ où $k$ est un entier naturel.

paraphrase.text: Find all pairs of positive integers $(m, q)$ such that $q$ is a prime number and $m^k - m = q$ for some non-negative integer $k$.

style.text: Soit $p$ un nombre premier. Trouver tous les entiers $x \geq 1$ tels que $x$ divise $x+p$ et que le quotient $\frac{x+p}{x}$ soit une puissance de $x$.

exact.text: Déterminer tous les couples d'entiers $(n, k)$ satisfaisant l'équation $(n^2 - 3)^2 - 8 = 7 \cdot 2^k$.

paraphrase.text: Déterminer tous les couples d'entiers $(n, k)$ satisfaisant l'équation $(n^2-3)^2 - 8 = 7 \cdot 2^k$.

style.text: Determine all pairs of integers $(m, n)$ such that $m^2(m^2-6) = 7 \cdot 2^n - 1$.

exact.text: Soit $k = 117819$ et $a = 2014$. Démontrer que la somme $\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} 4a \cdot 10^{4j}$ est un multiple de $a^3$.

paraphrase.text: Soit $m = 117819$ et $a = 2014$. Démontrer que l'expression $4 a \sum_{k=0}^{m-1} (10^4)^k$ est un multiple de $a^3$.

style.text: Soit $x = \sum_{j=0}^{117818} 10^{4j}$. Démontrer que l'entier $m = 8056 \cdot x$ est un multiple de $2014^3$.

exact.text: Déterminer l'ensemble des applications $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfaisant la relation $f(u) f(v) = u + f(u f(v-1))$ pour tout couple de réels $(u, v)$.

paraphrase.text: Determine all functions $g: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $u, v \in \mathbb{R}$, the identity $g(u) g(v) = u + g(u g(v-1))$ holds.

style.text: Déterminer toutes les fonctions $g: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfaisant l'égalité $g(u)g(v+1) - g(u g(v)) = u$ pour tout couple de réels $(u, v)$.

exact.text:
Soient $x, y, z$ des réels strictement positifs. Démontrer l'inégalité suivante :
$$\frac{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}{xyz} \geq 2 \left( \frac{xy + xz - yz}{xyz} \right)$$ 
 sachant que l'ordre des variables peut être permuté pour correspondre à la forme cyclique.

paraphrase.text: Démontrer que pour tous réels $x, y, z > 0$, l'inégalité $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \geq 2yz + 2xz - 2xy$ est vérifiée.

style.text: Let $x, y, z$ be positive real numbers. Prove the inequality $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \geq 2yz + 2xz - 2xy$.

exact.text: Soient $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 2}$. Supposons que pour tout entier $x$ tel que $1 \le x \le n$, la classe $\bar{x}$ soit un élément d'ordre divisant $n$ dans le groupe multiplicatif des restes modulo $m$. Démontrer que $n+1 = m$ et que $m$ appartient à l'ensemble des nombres premiers.

paraphrase.text: Suppose $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $m, n \ge 2$. If every element of the set $S = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ is a root of the polynomial $f(x) = x^n - 1$ in the ring of integers modulo $m$, show that $m$ is a prime number and $n = m-1$.

style.text: Soient $k, p$ deux entiers supérieurs ou égaux à $2$. On suppose que l'ordre multiplicatif de chaque élément de l'ensemble $S = \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ modulo $p$ divise $k$. Démontrer que $p$ est nécessairement un nombre premier tel que $p = k + 1$.

exact.text: Soit une suite finie d'entiers naturels $S = (s_k)_{k=1}^n$ avec $n=2019$. Démontrer que $S$ peut être représentée sous la forme $s_k = \lfloor k \alpha \rfloor$ pour une certaine constante réelle $\alpha$ si et seulement si la suite est sous-additive et presque sur-additive au sens suivant : pour tous indices $m, n$ tels que $m+n \leq 2019$, l'expression $s_{m+n} - s_m - s_n$ appartient à l'ensemble $\{0, 1\}$.

paraphrase.text: Soit $n = 2019$ et $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ une suite d'entiers strictement positifs. Prouver que l'intersection des intervalles $[\frac{a_k}{k}, \frac{a_k+1}{k})$ pour $k=1, \dots, n$ est non vide si et seulement si la condition $0 \le a_{i+j} - a_i - a_j \le 1$ est satisfaite pour tous indices $i, j$ tels que $i+j \le n$.

style.text: Let $S$ be a sequence of $n$ positive integers $s_1, s_2, \dots, s_n$. Prove that the sequence satisfies $s_i + s_j \le s_{i+j} \le s_i + s_j + 1$ for all indices such that $1 \le i, j, i+j \le n$ if and only if there exists a constant $\alpha$ such that $s_k = \lfloor k\alpha \rfloor$ for all $1 \le k \le n$.

exact.text: Déterminer l'ensemble des entiers naturels non nuls $n$ possédant la propriété suivante : pour tout $a \in \mathbb{Z}^{+}$, la condition $p \mid (a^n - 1)$ implique nécessairement $p^2 \mid (a^n - 1)$, où $p$ est un nombre premier fixé.

paraphrase.text: Given a prime $p$, identify the set of all positive integers $k$ with the property that the congruence $x^k \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ is satisfied by every integer $x$ that satisfies $x^k \equiv 1 \pmod p$.

style.text: Determine all positive integers $k$ such that for a fixed prime $q$, the condition $q \mid (m^k - 1)$ implies $q^2 \mid (m^k - 1)$ for every positive integer $m$.

exact.text:
Let $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy the congruence $4n \equiv -3 \pmod{11}$. 
(i) Express $n$ in the form $11k + r$, where $0 \le r < 11$.
(ii) Determine the value of $n^4 \pmod{11}$.

paraphrase.text:
Let $n$ be an integer such that $4n \equiv -3 \pmod{11}$. 
(i) Determine the general solution for $n$ in terms of an integer parameter $k$.
(ii) Calculate the residue of $n^4$ modulo $11$.

style.text: Let $k$ be an integer such that $11$ divides $4k - 8$. Determine the general expression for $k$ and calculate the remainder when $k^4$ is divided by $11$.

exact.text: In $\triangle ABC$, let $L$ be the angle bisector of $\angle A$. Let $I_1$ and $I_2$ denote the incenters of the two triangles formed by $L$ dividing $\triangle ABC$. If the line $I_1 I_2$ intersects the sides $AB$ and $AC$ at points $M$ and $N$, prove that the segments $BN$, $CM$, and $L$ are concurrent.

paraphrase.text: In $\triangle ABC$, let $L$ be the point on $BC$ such that $\angle BAL = \angle CAL$. Let $I_1$ and $I_2$ be the centers of the inscribed circles of $\triangle ABL$ and $\triangle ACL$, respectively. If the line $I_1 I_2$ intersects the segments $AB$ at $P$ and $AC$ at $Q$, prove that the lines $BQ$, $CP$, and $AL$ are concurrent.

style.text: In $\triangle PQR$, the angle bisector of $\angle P$ meets $QR$ at $S$. Let $I_1$ and $I_2$ be the centers of the circles inscribed in $\triangle PQS$ and $\triangle PRS$, respectively. The line $I_1 I_2$ intersects the sides $PQ$ and $PR$ at points $X$ and $Y$. Prove that the segments $QY$ and $RX$ intersect at a point $Z$ lying on the segment $PS$.

exact.text: Let $x_1, x_2, x_3 \in \mathbb{R}^+$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^3 x_i = 6$. Find the maximum of $\sum_{cyc} \sqrt[3]{x_1^2 + 2x_2x_3}$.

paraphrase.text:
Let $x, y, z$ be positive real numbers such that $x+y+z=1$. Find the maximum value of the sum
$$ T = \sqrt[3]{36} \left( \sqrt[3]{x^2 + 2yz} + \sqrt[3]{y^2 + 2zx} + \sqrt[3]{z^2 + 2xy} \right). $$

style.text: Let $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}^+$ such that $x+y+z=6$. Find the maximum possible value of the sum $\sum_{cyc} \sqrt[3]{(x+y+z)x - (xy+xz-2yz)}$.

exact.text: Let $k$ be an integer such that $7$ divides $3k + 8$. Determine the value of $r \in \{0, 1, \dots, 6\}$ such that $k \equiv r \pmod{7}$. Furthermore, find the residue of $k^n$ modulo $7$ for any integer $n \geq 2$ in terms of $n$.

paraphrase.text: Let $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy the congruence $3n \equiv -1 \pmod{7}$. Determine the value of $r \in \{0, 1, \dots, 6\}$ such that $n \equiv r \pmod{7}$, and find the residue of $n^k$ modulo $7$ for all integers $k \ge 2$.

style.text: Let $k$ be an integer such that $3k \equiv -1 \pmod{7}$. Determine the remainder when $k$ is divided by $7$, and find all possible values for $k^n \pmod{7}$ where $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ and $n \ge 2$.

exact.text: Find all integer pairs $(a, b) \in \{1, 2, \dots, 36\}^2$ such that for some $m \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, the identity $11 \left( \frac{a}{\gcd(a,m)} + \frac{b}{\gcd(b,m)} \right) = 10(a+b)$ holds.

paraphrase.text: Let $m \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. Find all ordered pairs $(u, v) \in \{1, 2, \dots, 36\}^2$ such that the identity $11(\operatorname{lcm}(u, m) + \operatorname{lcm}(v, m)) = 10m(u + v)$ holds.

style.text: Let $L(x,y)$ denote the least common multiple of $x$ and $y$. Find all pairs $(x,y) \in \mathbb{Z}^+ \times \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that $1 \le x, y \le 36$ and there exists a positive integer $k$ for which $11(L(x,k) + L(y,k)) = 10k(x+y)$.

exact.text:
Let $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers such that $ab+bc+ca=1$. Find the maximum value of $M$ such that the inequality
$$
\sum_{cyc} \frac{a^2}{a+abc} \ge M
$$ \nholds for all such $a, b, c$.

paraphrase.text: Let $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers such that $ab+bc+ca=1$. Find the maximum value of $K$ such that $$\sum_{cyc} \frac{a^2}{a+bc} \ge K.$$

style.text: Let $a, b,$ and $c$ be positive real numbers such that $ab + bc + ca = 1$. Find the minimum possible value of the sum: $$\frac{a^2}{a+bc} + \frac{b^2}{b+ca} + \frac{c^2}{c+ab}$$

exact.text:
Let $S$ be a set of $n$ distinct points on a circle. Assume that every set of four points from $S$ determines a unique intersection point of chords inside the circle. 
\ni. Determine $n$ such that $\binom{n}{3} = 2n$.
\nii. Determine $n$ such that the number of ways to choose a subset of four points from $S$ is exactly $5n$.

paraphrase.text:
Let $S$ be a set of $n$ distinct points on a circle. Assume the points are in general position such that no three diagonals of the convex $n$-gon formed by these points are concurrent. 
\ni. Determine $n$ such that $\binom{n}{3} = 2n$.
\nii. Determine $n$ such that the number of ways to choose a subset of 4 points from $S$ is exactly $5n$.

style.text: A convex polygon with $k$ vertices is drawn. No three diagonals are concurrent at any point other than a vertex. \\ i. If the number of distinct subsets of 3 vertices is $2k$, determine $k$. \\ ii. If the total number of intersection points of the diagonals inside the polygon is $5k$, determine $k$.

exact.text: Determine all $P \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ such that the identity $x(x-2)P(x+2) = (x+2)(x+4)P(x)$ holds for every real number $x$.

paraphrase.text: Determine all real polynomials $Q(y)$ such that $(y^2 - 2y)Q(y + 2) = (y^2 + 6y + 8)Q(y)$ holds for every real number $y$.

style.text: Determine all $Q \in \mathbb{R}[t]$ such that the identity $t(t-2) Q(t+2) = (t+2)(t+4) Q(t)$ holds for all real $t$.

exact.text: Find all triples $(x, y, p) \in \mathbb{Z}^+ \times \mathbb{Z}^+ \times \mathbb{P}$ such that $x = \frac{py}{y^3 - p}$, where $\mathbb{P}$ denotes the set of prime numbers.

paraphrase.text: Find all triples $(a, b, q) \in \mathbb{Z}^+ \times \mathbb{Z}^+ \times \mathbb{P}$ that satisfy the equality $a b^3 - q a - q b = 0$, where $\mathbb{P}$ denotes the set of prime numbers.

style.text: Find all triples of positive integers $(a, b, q)$ such that $q$ is a prime number and $a b^3 = q(a + b)$.

exact.text:
Let $\alpha = \frac{\sqrt{17}-1}{2}$. Consider a polynomial $f(x) \in \mathbb{N}[x]$ such that $f(\alpha) = 2017$. 
(i) Show that $f(1)$ is an odd integer.
(ii) Determine the minimum possible value of $f(1)$.

paraphrase.text: Let $\alpha = \frac{\sqrt{17}-1}{2}$. For a polynomial $f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^n c_k x^k$ with $c_k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$, given $f(\alpha) = 2017$, show that $f(1)$ is odd and determine the minimum value of $f(1)$.

style.text:
Given $\alpha = \frac{\sqrt{17}-1}{2}$, let $Q(x) = \sum_{i=0}^m c_i x^i$ be a polynomial with coefficients $c_i \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ such that $Q(\alpha) = 2017$. 
(a) Show that $\sum_{i=0}^m c_i$ is odd.
(b) Determine the minimum value of $Q(1)$.

exact.text: Given a sequence of rational numbers defined by $q_{k+1} = q_k(3q_k^2 + 1)$ with $q_1 = \frac{u}{v}$ where $\gcd(v, 3) = 1$. Show that if there exists an index $j \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that $\sqrt{q_j} \in \mathbb{Q}$, then $\sqrt{q_1} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

paraphrase.text: Given a sequence $a_1, a_2, \dots$ of rational numbers satisfying $a_{k+1} = a_k(3a_k^2 + 1)$ for all $k \ge 1$, let the initial term be $a_1 = \frac{p}{q}$ with $\gcd(q, 3) = 1$. Show that if there exists $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that $\sqrt{a_n} \in \mathbb{Q}$, then $\sqrt{a_1} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

style.text: A sequence of rational numbers $u_n$ is defined by $u_1 = q$ and $u_{k+1} = u_k(3u_k^2 + 1)$ for $k \ge 1$. Suppose there exists an index $j \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that $u_j = v^2$ for some $v \in \mathbb{Q}$. If the denominator of $q$ in simplest form is not a multiple of $3$, show that $q$ must be the square of a rational number.

exact.text: Let $h_b$ and $h_c$ be the altitudes from vertices $B$ and $C$ in $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle A = 60^\circ$. If $AD$ bisects $\angle A$ and the inradii of $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ADC$ are $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$, prove that $\frac{1}{\rho_1} + \frac{1}{\rho_2} = \frac{2}{r} + \frac{2 \sin 60^\circ}{h_c} + \frac{2 \sin 60^\circ}{h_b}$, where $r$ is the inradius of $\triangle ABC$.

paraphrase.text: Let $P$ be a point on the segment $QR$ of triangle $PQR$ such that $QP$ bisects $\angle QPR = \pi/3$. If $h, k$ are the side lengths $PR, PQ$ and $\rho_1, \rho_2, \rho$ are the inradii of $\triangle QPP$, $\triangle RPP$, and $\triangle PQR$ respectively, prove that $2(\rho^{-1} + h^{-1} + k^{-1}) = \rho_1^{-1} + \rho_2^{-1}$.

style.text: In $\triangle XYZ$, let $X = 60^\circ$ and let $W$ be a point on $YZ$ such that $XW$ bisects $\angle X$. Let $r_1$ be the radius of the circle inscribed in $\triangle XYW$, $r_2$ be the radius of the circle inscribed in $\triangle XZW$, and $R$ be the radius of the circle inscribed in $\triangle XYZ$. Prove that $\frac{1}{r_1} + \frac{1}{r_2} = \frac{2}{R} + \frac{2}{XY} + \frac{2}{XZ}$.

exact.text: Determine the set of all primes $p$ for which the equation $\sum_{k=1}^3 (n_k^p - n_k) = q_1 q_2 q_3$ has a solution in non-negative integers $n_1, n_2, n_3$ and distinct primes $q_1, q_2, q_3$.

paraphrase.text: Determine all primes $q$ such that for some $a, b, c \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$, the expression $\sum_{i \in \{a,b,c\}} (i^q - i)$ can be written as $p_1 p_2 p_3$ where $p_1, p_2, p_3$ are three different prime integers.

style.text: Determine all primes $q$ such that the set $S = \{a, b, c\} \subset \mathbb{N}_0$ satisfies the condition that $\sum_{k \in S} (k^q - k)$ is the product of three different primes.

exact.text: Given a subset $S = \{n_1, n_2, \dots, n_k\} \subset \mathbb{Z}^+$ with $n_1 < n_2 < \dots < n_k$ and $k \ge 2$, suppose no element $x \in S$ is the sum of elements from any subset $T \subseteq S \setminus \{x\}$ with $|T| \ge 2$. Show that for each $j \in \{1, 2, \dots, k-1\}$, the inequality $j n_j + n_k \ge (j+1)(k-1)$ holds.

paraphrase.text: Given a set of $n \ge 2$ positive integers $X = \{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n\}$ ordered such that $x_1 < x_2 < \dots < x_n$, assume that for every $k \in \{1, \dots, n\}$, $x_k \notin \{ \sum_{i \in I} x_i : I \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\} \setminus \{k\}, |I| \ge 2 \}$. Show that for all $1 \le j < n$, the inequality $j x_j + x_n \ge (j+1)(n-1)$ is satisfied.

style.text: A collection of $n \ge 2$ distinct positive integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ is sorted such that $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_n$. It is known that no element in the collection is the sum of a subset of the other elements of size at least 2. Show that for any index $k \in \{1, 2, \dots, n-1\}$, the inequality $k a_k + a_n \ge (k+1)(n-1)$ holds.

exact.text: Find all $f: (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ such that the expression $f(xf(y)) - xy$ is equal to $yz + zx - yf(z) - zf(x)$ for every triple of positive real numbers $(x, y, z)$.

paraphrase.text: Find all $f: (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying $f(af(b)) + bf(c) + cf(a) = ab + bc + ca$ for all $a, b, c > 0$.

style.text: Find all functions $g: (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying the identity $g(a g(b)) - ab = b(c - g(c)) + c(a - g(a))$ for all positive real numbers $a, b, c$.

exact.text:
(A) Let $S_1 = a+b+c$ and $S_2 = ab+bc+ca$ for $a,b,c \in \mathbb{R}$. Show that $S_1^2 - 3S_2 \ge 0$, and determine the condition for $S_1^2 = 3S_2$. 

(B) Suppose $u, v, w$ are positive reals such that $\frac{1}{vw} + \frac{1}{wu} + \frac{1}{uv} = \frac{1}{\alpha}$ and $\frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{w} = \frac{1}{\beta}$ for some constants $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$. Prove that $\alpha \ge 3\beta^2$, identifying the case of equality.

paraphrase.text: (A) For any $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$, show that $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 \ge ab + bc + ca$, and determine the condition for equality. (B) Suppose $u, v, w > 0$ satisfy $\frac{1}{vw} + \frac{1}{wu} + \frac{1}{uv} = \frac{1}{\alpha}$ and $\frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{w} = \frac{1}{\beta}$ for constants $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$. Show that $\alpha \ge 3\beta^2$ and find the equality case.

style.text: Let $u, v, w$ be positive real numbers. Define $p = \frac{uvw}{u+v+w}$ and $q = \frac{uvw}{uv+vw+wu}$. Show that the inequality $p \ge 3q^2$ always holds, and identify the condition for equality.

exact.text: Let $e_1 = a+b+c$ and $e_2 = ab+bc+ca$ for $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$. If $\max(|a-b|, |b-c|, |c-a|) > \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$, show that the quadratic $Q(x) = x^2 - 4e_1 x + 12e_2$ takes a negative value for at least one $x \in \mathbb{Z}$.

paraphrase.text: Let $u, v, w \in \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that $\max\{|u-v|, |v-w|, |w-u|\} > \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$. Show that the open interval defined by the inequality $x^2 - 4(u+v+w)x + 12(uv+vw+wu) < 0$ contains at least one integer.

style.text: Let $p, q, r \in \mathbb{R}$. Given that $\max\{|p-q|, |q-r|, |r-p|\} > \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$, show that there is some $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ satisfying $n^2 - 4(p+q+r)n + 12(pq+qr+rp) < 0$.

exact.text: Let $S = \{ k \in \mathbb{Z}^+ : n \mid (2^n + 1) \}$. Show that $|S| = \aleph_0$ and determine the set $S \cap \mathbb{P}$, where $\mathbb{P}$ denotes the set of prime numbers.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \{ k \in \mathbb{Z}^+ : 2^k \equiv -1 \pmod{k} \}$. Demonstrate that $S$ is an infinite set, and identify the set $S \cap \mathbb{P}$, where $\mathbb{P}$ denotes the set of prime numbers.

style.text: Let $S = \{k \in \mathbb{Z}^+ : 2^k \equiv -1 \pmod{k}\}$. Show that $S$ is an infinite set, and determine all elements of $S$ that have exactly two positive divisors.

exact.text: For two triangles with angles $\alpha_1, \beta_1, \gamma_1$ and $\alpha_2, \beta_2, \gamma_2$, show that if $m, n \ge 1$, then the following inequality holds: $\sin^m \alpha_1 \sin^n \alpha_2 + \sin^m \beta_1 \sin^n \beta_2 + \sin^m \gamma_1 \sin^n \gamma_2 \le \frac{9}{4}$.

paraphrase.text:
Given two triangles with angles $(\alpha_1, \beta_1, \gamma_1)$ and $(\alpha_2, \beta_2, \gamma_2)$, and diameters of their circumcircles $D_1$ and $D_2$ respectively, show that for any real $p, q \ge 1$:
$$\sum_{\text{cyc}} (D_1 \sin \alpha_1)^p (D_2 \sin \alpha_2)^q \le \frac{9}{4} D_1^p D_2^q$$

style.text: In two triangles $T_1$ and $T_2$, let the side lengths be $x, y, z$ and $u, v, w$ respectively, with circumradii $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$. Show that for any exponents $p, q \in [1, \infty)$, the following inequality holds: $x^p u^q + y^p v^q + z^p w^q \le 2^{p+q-2} \cdot 9 \rho_1^p \rho_2^q$.

exact.text: Let $G$ be a simple graph with 6 vertices. Demonstrate that either the clique number $\omega(G) \ge 3$ or the independence number $\alpha(G) \ge 3$.

paraphrase.text: Let $K_6$ be a complete graph on 6 vertices where every edge is colored either red or blue. Prove that there exists at least one monochromatic triangle in the graph.

style.text: Let $S$ be a set of 6 points in the plane such that no three points are collinear. Each segment connecting two points in $S$ is colored either crimson or indigo. Show that there exists a triangle with vertices in $S$ whose three sides have the same color.

exact.text: Let $n \ge 5$ be an integer. Suppose $P(x) \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ satisfies $P(i) \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ for all $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n\}$. Prove that $P(0) = P(1) = \dots = P(n)$.

paraphrase.text: Let $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $n \ge 5$. Suppose $P(y) \in \mathbb{Z}[y]$ has the property that for all $j \in \{1, 2, \dots, n+1\}$, the value $P(j)$ lies in the interval $[0, n-1]$. Show that $P(1) = P(2) = \dots = P(n+1)$.

style.text: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 3. Suppose a polynomial $P(x) \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ satisfies $|2P(j) - n| \le n$ for all $j \in \{0, 1, \dots, n+1\}$. Show that $P(0) = P(1) = \dots = P(n+1)$.

exact.text: Consider a complete graph $K_n$ with $n$ vertices where $n \ge 3$. Suppose each edge is assigned a color from the set $C = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. We say a set of three vertices is 'trichromatic' if the three edges connecting them are assigned three distinct colors. Find all $n$ such that for every subset $S \subset C$ with $|S|=3$, there exists a trichromatic triangle whose edges have colors in $S$.

paraphrase.text: Consider a complete graph $K_n$ with $n \ge 3$ vertices, where each edge is assigned a color from the set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. Suppose that for every subset of three distinct colors $S \subset \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, there is a triangle in $K_n$ whose edges are colored with the elements of $S$. Find all possible values of $n$.

style.text: A network consists of $k$ servers ($k \ge 3$). Every pair of servers is connected by a direct link, and each link is assigned one of $k$ possible encryption protocols. It is observed that for every set of three distinct protocols, there is a trio of servers such that the three links connecting them utilize exactly those three protocols. Find all possible values of $k$.

exact.text: For a prime $p$, let $n = qp + r$ where $q, r \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $0 \le r < p$. Prove that $\binom{qp+r}{p} \equiv q \pmod{p}$.

paraphrase.text: For any prime $q$ and integer $m \in \{q, q+1, \dots\}$, prove that $\binom{m}{q} \equiv k \pmod{q}$, where $m = kq + r$ with $0 \le r < q$.

style.text: Let $S$ be a set with $m$ elements. For any prime $q \le m$, let $N$ be the number of ways to choose a subset of size $q$ from $S$. If $m = aq + r$ with $0 \le r < q$, prove that $N \equiv a \pmod{q}$.

exact.text: Let $a = 2005$. Prove that the set $S = \{ n \in \mathbb{Z}^+ : \mu(n) \neq 0 \text{ and } n \mid a^n - 1 \}$ is infinite, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function.

paraphrase.text: Prove that the set of positive integers $k$ satisfying $2005^k \equiv 1 \pmod{k}$ contains infinitely many elements that are not divisible by the square of any prime.

style.text: Let $S$ be the set of all squarefree natural numbers $k$ such that $k \equiv 1 \pmod{\text{ord}_k(3)}$. Prove that $S$ is an infinite set.

exact.text: Given a sequence of positive reals $\{x_k\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ and a constant $C > 0$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2 \leq C x_{n+1}^2$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, show that the partial sums $S_n = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i$ satisfy $S_n = O(x_{n+1})$.

paraphrase.text: Suppose $(x_k)_{k \geq 1}$ is a sequence of positive reals. Given that the partial sums of the squares satisfy $\sum_{k=1}^n x_k^2 = O(x_{n+1}^2)$, show that the partial sums of the terms themselves satisfy $\sum_{k=1}^n x_k = O(x_{n+1})$.

style.text: Given a sequence of positive reals $\{x_k\}_{k \ge 1}$, let $S_n = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2$. Suppose the ratio $S_n / x_{n+1}^2$ is bounded from above for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. Show that there exists a constant $C$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i < C x_{n+1}$ for all $n \ge 1$.

exact.text: Let $\sigma \in S_{10}$ be a permutation of the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 10\}$. Define the cyclic sum $f(\sigma) = \sum_{i=1}^{10} |2\sigma(i) - 3\sigma(i+1)|$, where $\sigma(11) = \sigma(1)$. Determine the size of the set $\{ \sigma \in S_{10} : f(\sigma) = \max_{\tau \in S_{10}} f(\tau) \}$.

paraphrase.text: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 10\}$. Consider the cyclic sum $C(\sigma) = \sum_{i=1}^{10} |2\sigma(i) - 3\sigma(i+1)|$, where $\sigma(11) = \sigma(1)$. Determine the size of the set $\{\sigma \in S_{10} : C(\sigma) = \max_{\tau \in S_{10}} C(\tau)\}$.

style.text: Ten students are seated at a round table, and each is assigned a unique ID number from the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 10\}$. Let $v_i$ denote the ID of the student at seat $i$ (where seat $11$ is seat $1$). A judge calculates a total score by summing the values $f(v_i, v_{i+1}) = |3v_{i+1} - 2v_i|$ for $i=1, 2, \dots, 10$. How many distinct assignments of ID numbers to seats result in the maximum possible total score?

exact.text: Let $\mathcal{P} = \{p \in \mathbb{Z}^+ : p \text{ is prime}, p < 101\}$. For each $p \in \mathcal{P}$, prove that the set $S_p = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{Z}_p^2 : x^3 - y^{37} + 11 \equiv 0 \pmod{p}\}$ is non-empty.

paraphrase.text: Prove that for any prime $q \in \{2, 3, \dots, 97\}$, there exist integers $u$ and $v$ such that $v^{37} - u^3 \equiv 11 \pmod{q}$.

style.text: Let $S = \{2, 3, 5, \dots, 97\}$ be the set of primes less than $100$. Prove that for each $q \in S$, there exist integers $a$ and $b$ such that $a^3 - b^{37} + 11 \equiv 0 \pmod{q}$.

exact.text: Let $S$ be the set of all integers $m > 1$ such that the value $1$ can be represented as the sum of exactly $2011$ terms of the form $m^{-k}$, where each $k$ is a non-negative integer. Calculate the number of elements in $S$.

paraphrase.text: Find the count of all $m \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that $1 = \sum_{j=1}^{2011} m^{k_j}$ has a solution for some integers $k_1, k_2, \dots, k_{2011} \in \mathbb{Z}$.

style.text: A sequence of $2011$ non-negative integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{2011}$ is chosen. Find the number of possible values of $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that $n^k = \sum_{i=1}^{2011} n^{a_i}$ for some integer $k \ge 0$.

exact.text: Consider the set of points $\mathcal{P} = \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\} \times \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Determine the number of subsets $T \subset \mathcal{P}$ such that $|T|=3$ and the elements of $T$ are not collinear.

paraphrase.text: Let $A = \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$. Determine the number of subsets $T \subset A \times A$ such that $|T| = 3$ and the elements of $T$ do not lie on a common line.

style.text: In a $6 \times 6$ square array of dots, how many distinct subsets of three dots do not lie on a common line?

exact.text: Let $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ and let $M_{AB}$ and $M_{AC}$ be the midpoints of the arcs $AB$ and $AC$ not containing $C$ and $B$, respectively. Let $M'_{AB}$ and $M'_{AC}$ be the reflections of these arc midpoints across their respective chords $AB$ and $AC$. If $O$ is the center of $\Omega$ and $H$ is the orthocenter of $\triangle ABC$, show that the points $M'_{AB}, A, M'_{AC}$ lie on a common line if and only if the points $O, H, M'_{AB}, M'_{AC}$ lie on a common circle.

paraphrase.text: Let $R$ be the circumradius and $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$, where $b > a > c$. Let $M_c$ and $M_b$ be the midpoints of the arcs $AB$ and $AC$ not containing $C$ and $B$, respectively. Define $P$ such that $\vec{M_c P} = 2 \text{proj}_{\vec{AB}^\perp}(\vec{M_c A})$ and $Q$ such that $\vec{M_b Q} = 2 \text{proj}_{\vec{AC}^\perp}(\vec{M_b A})$. Show that the points $O, H, P, Q$ lie on a common circle if and only if $A$ lies on the line segment $PQ$.

style.text: In $\triangle XYZ$ with $XZ > YZ > XY$, let $S$ be the center of the circumscribed circle and $T$ be the intersection of the altitudes. Let $P$ and $Q$ be the midpoints of the minor arcs $XY$ and $XZ$ respectively. Points $P^*$ and $Q^*$ are defined such that $XY$ is the perpendicular bisector of $PP^*$ and $XZ$ is the perpendicular bisector of $QQ^*$. Show that $S, T, P^*, Q^*$ lie on a common circle if and only if $X$ lies on the segment $P^*Q^*$.

exact.text: Evaluate $S \pmod{100}$, where $S = \sum_{k=0}^{2014} \frac{2^k - (2^k \pmod 3)}{3}$.

paraphrase.text: Evaluate the sum $S = \sum_{k=0}^{2014} \frac{2^k - (2^k \pmod 3)}{3}$ and determine the residue of $S$ modulo $100$.

style.text: Calculate the value of $S = \sum_{k=0}^{2014} \frac{2^k - a_k}{3} \pmod{100}$, where $a_k \in \{1, 2\}$ is the remainder when $2^k$ is divided by $3$.

exact.text: Let $P$ be a point on side $AC$ of $\triangle ABC$ with $AB=13$ and $BC=7$. If there exists a point $Q$ on segment $AB$ such that $BQ=7$ and the ray $EP$ bisects $\angle CED$ where $D=Q$ and $E=P$, determine the product of all possible lengths of $AE$.

paraphrase.text: In $\triangle ABC$, let $c = 13$ and $a = 7$. Points $D$ and $E$ lie on segments $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. Given that the length of segment $BD$ is equal to $a$, and that $EB$ bisects $\angle DEC$, determine the product of all possible lengths of $AE$.

style.text: In \triangle PQR, PQ = 13 and QR = 7. Let S be a point on the side PQ such that QS = 7, and let T be a point on PR such that QT bisects \angle STR. Determine the product of all possible lengths of PT.

exact.text: For $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$, if the quadratic $f(t) = t^2 + mt + n$ vanishes at $t = m + n$, determine the minimum of the product $mn$.

paraphrase.text: Given two integers $m$ and $n$, suppose that the quadratic polynomial $f(z) = z^2 + mz + n$ vanishes at $z = m + n$. Determine the minimum achievable value of the product $mn$.

style.text: Given two integers $m$ and $n$, suppose that the quadratic expression $P(x) = x^2 + mx + n$ vanishes when $x = m + n$. Determine the minimum possible product of $m$ and $n$.

exact.text: Let $M$ be a $10 \times 10$ matrix where each entry $m_{i,j}$ is an element of a set of colors $S$. If the image of every row vector and every column vector under the set-representation function has a cardinality of at most $5$, find the maximum possible value of $|S|$.

paraphrase.text: Let $A$ be a $10 \times 10$ matrix where each entry $a_{i,j}$ is an element from a set of symbols $S$. If the size of the set $\{a_{i,j} : 1 \le j \le 10\}$ is at most 5 for every $i \in \{1, \dots, 10\}$, and the size of the set $\{a_{i,j} : 1 \le i \le 10\}$ is at most 5 for every $j \in \{1, \dots, 10\}$, find the maximum possible cardinality of the set of all entries $\{a_{i,j} : 1 \le i, j \le 10\}$.

style.text: A $10 \times 10$ array of light bulbs is installed on a wall. Each bulb can be set to one of $N$ possible wavelengths. If every row and every column is restricted to containing at most 5 distinct wavelengths, what is the largest possible value of $N$?

exact.text: Let $S = \{0, 1, 2, 7\}$. Determine the number of sequences $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_k)$ such that $d_i \in S$ for all $i$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k d_i \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$. (Note: The case $n=10^k$ is excluded because its digits are not all in $S$.)

paraphrase.text: Given $k \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, determine the number of sequences $(d_0, d_1, \dots, d_{k-1})$ where each $d_i \in \{0, 1, 2, 7\}$ such that $\sum_{i=0}^{k-1} d_i \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$. (Note: The case where all $d_i=0$ corresponds to $n=0$, and $10^k$ is excluded as its digits are not in the set.)

style.text: A sequence of length $m$ is formed using elements from the set $\{0, 1, 2, 7\}$. How many such sequences $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_m)$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^m d_i \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$? Note that the number $10^m$ is also considered a valid value if it meets the conditions.

exact.text: Determine the maximum cardinality $n$ of a set of distinct positive values $S = \{y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n\}$ such that for all $y_i, y_j \in S$, the expression $4y_iy_j - 3(y_i^2 + y_j^2)$ is at least as large as $1 - 2y_iy_j + y_i^2y_j^2$.

paraphrase.text: Determine the maximum value of $n$ for which one can find $n$ distinct elements in $\mathbb{R}^+$ such that for every pair of distinct indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, n\}$, the expression $x_i^2 x_j^2 + 8x_ix_j + 1$ is at most $3(x_i^2 + x_j^2)$.

style.text: Determine the maximum number of elements in a set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^+$ such that for every pair of distinct elements $a, b \in S$, the condition $3(a^2 + b^2) \ge 1 + 8ab + a^2b^2$ is satisfied.

exact.text: Let $S = \sum_{k=n+1}^{2n+8} \frac{1}{k}$ where $n=1008$. Determine the value of $\lfloor 10(S - \lfloor S \rfloor) \rfloor$.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \sum_{k=1}^{1008} \frac{1}{k+1008}$. Determine the value of $\lfloor 10S \rfloor \pmod{10}$.

style.text: Let $S = \sum_{k=n+1}^{2n} \frac{1}{k+8}$ where $n=1008$. Determine the value of $\lfloor 10S \rfloor \pmod{10}$.

exact.text: Determine all sextuples of positive integers $(x_0, x_1, x_2, y_0, y_1, y_2)$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, the sum $\sum_{i=0}^2 (x_i^{2017n} + y_i)n^i$ is a multiple of $\sum_{i=0}^2 (x_i y_i)n^i$.

paraphrase.text: Determine all sextuples of positive integers $(x_0, x_1, x_2, y_0, y_1, y_2)$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, the congruence $\sum_{i=0}^2 (x_i^{2017n} + y_i)n^i \equiv 0 \pmod{\sum_{i=0}^2 x_i y_i n^i}$ holds.

style.text: Determine all sextuples of positive integers $(x_0, x_1, x_2, y_0, y_1, y_2)$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, the sum $\sum_{k=0}^2 (x_k^{2017n} + y_k)n^k$ is a multiple of $\sum_{k=0}^2 (x_k y_k)n^k$.

exact.text: Determine every sequence of non-negative integers $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_n$ such that $\sum_{i=0}^n a_i = 7$ and $\sum_{i=0}^n a_i 2^i = 2017$.

paraphrase.text: Determine all sequences of non-negative integers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ with finite support such that $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n = 7$ and $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n 2^n = 2017$.

style.text: A sequence of non-negative integers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$ satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^k a_i = 7$ and $\sum_{i=0}^k a_i 2^i = 2017$. Determine all possible sequences.

exact.text: Let $T$ be an isosceles triangle inscribed in a circle $C$ with base angles $\alpha$. If two points $P_1, P_2$ are sampled uniformly from the circumference of $C$, the probability that the segment $\overline{P_1 P_2}$ shares at least one point with $T$ is $0.56$. Determine the sum of all possible values of $\alpha$ in degrees.

paraphrase.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be an isosceles triangle inscribed in a circle $\mathcal{C}$ such that $\angle B = \angle C = x^\circ$. If two points $P$ and $Q$ are sampled uniformly and independently from the circumference of $\mathcal{C}$, the probability that the open line segment $PQ$ shares at least one point with the interior or boundary of $\triangle ABC$ is $0.56$. Determine the sum of all possible values of $x$.

style.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be an isosceles triangle inscribed in a circle $\mathcal{C}$ with $\angle B = \angle C = \theta^\circ$. A random chord $XY$ is formed by picking two points uniformly and independently on $\mathcal{C}$. Given that the probability that $XY$ contains at least one interior point of $\triangle ABC$ is $0.56$, find the sum of all possible values of $\theta$.

exact.text: Let $S = \{n \in \mathbb{Z} : 1 \le n \le 2019\}$. For any distinct $a, b \in S$, define $g(a, b) = \gcd(2^a + 1, 2^b + 1)$. Determine the sum of the elements in the set $\mathcal{V} = \{g(a, b) : a, b \in S, a \neq b\}$.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \{2^n + 1 \mid n \in \mathbb{Z}, 1 \le n \le 2019\}$. Calculate the sum of the elements in the set $\{ \gcd(x, y) : x, y \in S, x \neq y \}$.

style.text: Let $S = \{n \in \mathbb{Z} : 1 \le n \le 2019\}$. For any distinct $i, j \in S$, let $g_{i,j} = \gcd(2^i+1, 2^j+1)$. Determine the sum of all elements in the set $V = \{g_{i,j} : i, j \in S, i \neq j\}$.

exact.text: In an acute triangle $ABC$ with circumradius $R$, let $M$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ not containing $A$. If the distance from the incenter $I$ to $M$ satisfies $IM = R$, prove that the distance from the vertex $A$ to the orthocenter $H$ is at least the distance from $A$ to $I$.

paraphrase.text: In an acute triangle $ABC$ with circumcircle $\Gamma$ and circumradius $R$, let $I$ be the incenter and $H$ the orthocenter. Let $M$ be the point on $\Gamma$ such that $AM$ bisects $\angle BAC$. If the circle centered at $M$ passing through $B$ and $C$ has radius $R$, prove that the segment $AH$ is at least as long as $AI$.

style.text: In an acute triangle $XYZ$, let $O$ be the circumcenter and $W$ be the orthocenter. Let the angle bisector of $\angle YXZ$ intersect the circumcircle at $P$. If the distance from $P$ to the incenter $J$ is equal to the circumradius $R$, prove that the distance from $X$ to $W$ is at least the distance from $X$ to $J$.

exact.text: In $\triangle ABC$, let $\ell_B$ and $\ell_C$ be the external angle bisectors of $\angle B$ and $\angle C$. A circle $\Gamma$ passing through $B$ and $C$ intersects $\ell_B$ at $E$ and $\ell_C$ at $F$. Let $P = EF \cap AB$ and $Q = EF \cap AC$. Show that the intersection of the circumcircles of $\triangle BFP$ and $\triangle CEQ$ is a point whose coordinates depend only on the vertices $A, B, C$.

paraphrase.text: In $\triangle ABC$, let $BE$ and $CF$ be the external bisectors of $\angle B$ and $\angle C$, with $E$ and $F$ lying on a circle $\mathcal{K}$ that also passes through $B$ and $C$. Let the line $EF$ intersect the lines $AB$ and $AC$ at $P$ and $Q$. Show that there exists a point $X$ such that $X$ lies on the circumcircles of both $\triangle BFP$ and $\triangle CEQ$ for any choice of $\mathcal{K}$.

style.text: In $\triangle XYZ$, let $K$ be an interior point and $\omega$ be the circumcircle of $\triangle YZK$. Points $U$ and $V$ lie on $\omega$ such that $YU$ bisects the exterior angle at $Y$ and $ZV$ bisects the exterior angle at $Z$. Let the line $UV$ intersect the lines $XY$ and $XZ$ at $M$ and $N$, where $M$ is outside segment $XY$ and $N$ is outside segment $XZ$. Show that the intersection of the circumcircle of $\triangle YVM$ and the circumcircle of $\triangle ZUN$ is a point independent of the choice of $K$.

exact.text: In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, let the line tangent to the circumcircle at $D$ meet $BA$ and $BC$ at $E$ and $F$. Define $T$ as the unique point in $\triangle ABC$ satisfying $\vec{TE} \cdot \vec{CD}^\perp = 0$ and $\vec{TF} \cdot \vec{AD}^\perp = 0$. If $K$ lies on $DF$ such that $K \neq D$ and $\triangle TDK$ is isosceles with base $DK$, show that $BK$ passes through the intersection of $AC$ and $DT$.

paraphrase.text: In a cyclic quadrilateral $P_1 P_2 P_3 P_4$ with circumcircle $\Gamma$, let the line tangent to $\Gamma$ at $P_4$ meet the lines $P_2 P_1$ and $P_2 P_3$ at $X$ and $Y$. Suppose a point $Q$ satisfies $QX \parallel P_3 P_4$ and $QY \parallel P_1 P_4$. If $Z$ is the unique point on the segment $P_4 Y$ distinct from $P_4$ such that the triangle $Q P_4 Z$ is isosceles with $QP_4 = QZ$, show that $P_1 P_3$, $P_4 Q$, and $P_2 Z$ are concurrent.

style.text: In a cyclic quadrilateral $PQRS$ inscribed in $\Gamma$, the tangent at $S$ meets the extensions of $QP$ and $QR$ at $X$ and $Y$. Let $M$ be a point such that $MX \parallel RS$ and $MY \parallel PS$. If $Z$ is a point on the segment $SY$ distinct from $S$ such that $MS = MZ$, show that $PR, SM,$ and $QZ$ are concurrent.

exact.text: Let $S$ be a set of $n$ lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that no three lines are concurrent. If $k$ is the number of intersection points formed by these lines, determine the minimum value of $n$ for $k=2022$ and $k=2023$. Note that if $m$ lines are parallel to each other, they contribute zero intersections among themselves.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \{n_1, n_2, \dots, n_k\}$ be a multiset of positive integers such that no three lines in the plane are concurrent, and lines are parallel if and only if they belong to the same group $n_i$. Find the minimum sum $\sum_{i=1}^k n_i$ such that the sum of the products of all pairs $\sum_{1 \le i < j \le k} n_i n_j$ equals $M$, for $M=2022$ and $M=2023$.

style.text:
A set of $n$ distinct lines is drawn in the plane. Let $P$ be the number of points where at least two lines intersect. No three lines are concurrent. 

(i) Determine the minimum value of $n$ such that $P = 2022$.

(ii) Determine the minimum value of $n$ such that $P = 2023$.

exact.text: Let $S$ be the set of all positive integers $n$ such that there exist $d_1, d_2, d_3 \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ with $d_1 < d_2 < d_3$, $d_i \mid n$ for each $i$, and $\sum_{i=1}^3 d_i = 2022$. Find $\min S$.

paraphrase.text: Let $S$ be the set of all positive integers $n$ for which there exist three unique elements $x, y, z$ in the set of divisors of $n$ satisfying $x + y + z = 2022$. Find $\min S$.

style.text: Let $S$ be the set of all integers $n$ that possess a subset of divisors $\{d_1, d_2, d_3\}$ such that $d_1 < d_2 < d_3$ and $d_1 + d_2 + d_3 = 2022$. Find $\min S$.

exact.text: Let $S = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$. Construct two $4 \times 4$ Latin squares $L_1$ and $L_2$ over the symbol set $S$ such that the set of ordered pairs $\{(L_1(i,j), L_2(i,j)) : 1 \le i, j \le 4\}$ contains every element of $S \times S$ exactly once.

paraphrase.text: Construct two $4 \times 4$ Latin squares $S_1$ and $S_2$ using the symbol set $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ such that the set of ordered pairs $\{(S_1(i,j), S_2(i,j)) : 1 \le i, j \le 4\}$ contains all 16 possible elements of $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}^2$.

style.text: An organizer is placing 16 musicians into a $4 \times 4$ parade formation. Each musician belongs to one of four instrument groups (Strings, Brass, Woodwinds, Percussion) and one of four skill grades (Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, Elite). If each row and each column must contain exactly one musician from every instrument group and exactly one musician from every skill grade, and no two musicians share both the same instrument group and the same skill grade, describe a valid arrangement.

exact.text: Two players, $A$ and $B$, independently roll two fair six-sided dice. Let $S_A$ and $S_B$ be the sums of the outcomes for $A$ and $B$, respectively. Find the probability that the condition $S_A \equiv 0 \pmod{3} \lor S_B \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ is satisfied.

paraphrase.text: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be independent random variables representing the sums of two separate rolls of a pair of fair six-sided dice. Calculate the probability that the product $S_1 S_2$ is a multiple of $3$.

style.text: An urn contains $6$ balls labeled $1$ through $6$. Alice and Bob each draw two balls with replacement. Alice wins if the sum of her two numbers is a multiple of $3$, or if Bob's sum is a multiple of $3$. Otherwise, Bob wins. Find the probability that Alice wins.

exact.text: Find the sum of the squares of the roots of a cubic polynomial $P(x) = x^3 + px^2 + qx + r$ where the sum of the roots is $3$ and the sum of the products of the roots taken two at a time is $0$.

paraphrase.text: Suppose $a, b, c$ are the roots of the polynomial $P(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + d$ for some non-zero real constant $d$. Determine the value of $a^2 + b^2 + c^2$.

style.text: Consider three non-zero real numbers $x, y, z$ such that their arithmetic mean is $1$. If the sum of their pairwise products is zero, find the value of $x^2 + y^2 + z^2$.

exact.text: Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a set of $4k$ points on the perimeter of a square such that each edge, including its two endpoints, contains exactly $k+1$ points. Find the total number of subsets of $\mathcal{S}$ with cardinality 3 that do not consist of three collinear points.

paraphrase.text: Let $S$ be a set of $4k$ points located on the perimeter of a rectangle $ABCD$. The set $S$ includes the four corner points $A, B, C, D$, and each of the four segments $AB, BC, CD, DA$ contains exactly $k+1$ points from $S$. Calculate the number of subsets of $S$ of cardinality 3 that do not lie on a common line.

style.text: A grid of $4k$ decorative lights is arranged along the perimeter of a square courtyard. There is a light at each corner, and $k-1$ lights are spaced evenly along the edge between any two corners. If a technician chooses 3 distinct lights to form a circuit, how many sets of lights do not lie on a single straight line?

exact.text: Determine the number of unordered pairs of positive integers $\{a, b\}$ that satisfy the equation $\left(1 + \frac{1}{a}\right)\left(1 + \frac{1}{b}\right) = 1 + \frac{1}{2010}$.

paraphrase.text: Determine the number of unordered pairs of positive integers $\{a, b\}$ that satisfy the equation $\left(1 + \frac{1}{a}\right)\left(1 + \frac{1}{b}\right) = 1 + \frac{1}{2010}$.

style.text: Find the number of sets $\{x, y\} \subset \mathbb{Z}^+$ satisfying the equation $\frac{x+1}{x} \cdot \frac{y+1}{y} = 1 + \frac{1}{2010}$.

exact.text: Two circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ are tangent internally at $O$ with radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ ($r_1 < r_2$). A chord $XY$ of $\omega_2$ is parallel to the tangent at $O$, and its intersection with $\omega_1$ is $Z$, such that $X$ and $Z$ are on the same side of the diameter through $O$. Show that the circumradius of $\triangle OXZ$ is a constant $\rho$ and express $\rho$ using $r_1$ and $r_2$.

paraphrase.text: Two circles $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ are tangent at a point $O$, with $\mathcal{C}_1$ lying inside $\mathcal{C}_2$. Let $d_1$ and $d_2$ be their respective diameters. A chord $XY$ of $\mathcal{C}_2$ is drawn perpendicular to the line of centers such that it intersects $\mathcal{C}_1$ at a point $Z$. If $X$ and $Z$ are on the same side of the line of centers, show that the circumradius of $\triangle OZX$ is invariant as the chord $XY$ moves, and find this radius using $d_1$ and $d_2$.

style.text: Two circles $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ are tangent at the origin $O(0,0)$ and both lie in the upper half-plane, with diameters $d_1$ and $d_2$ along the $y$-axis ($d_1 < d_2$). A horizontal line $y = h$ intersects $\mathcal{C}_1$ at $P$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ at $Q$, where both points have positive $x$-coordinates. Find the circumradius of $\triangle OPQ$ in terms of $d_1$ and $d_2$.

exact.text: Find every ordered pair of primes $(x, y)$ such that the polynomial $f(t) = t^4 - x t^3 - y$ has at least one integer root.

paraphrase.text: Find all ordered pairs of primes $(m, n)$ such that the polynomial $f(x) = x^4 - m x^3 - n$ has at least one integer root.

style.text: Let $m$ and $n$ be prime numbers. Find all ordered pairs $(m, n)$ such that the polynomial $P(x) = x^4 - mx^3 - n$ has at least one integer root.

exact.text: Given $a \in \mathbb{R}$, find the sum of the roots of the polynomial $P(x) = (x-1)(x^2 + x - a^2 + a)$.

paraphrase.text: Given a real constant $k$, find the sum of the roots of the cubic polynomial $P(y) = y^3 + (k - k^2 - 1)y + k^2 - k$.

style.text: For a fixed constant $k \in \mathbb{R}$, find the sum of the roots of the cubic polynomial $P(y) = y^3 - (k^2-k+1)y + k^2 - k$.

exact.text: Let $p$ be a fixed prime. Find the set of all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ for which there exists some $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ satisfying the equality $n(n+p) = k^2$.

paraphrase.text: Let $p$ be a prime. Find the set of all integers $x$ for which the product $x(x+p)$ is a perfect square.

style.text: Let $q$ be a prime. Find all integer solutions $k$ to the equation $k^2 - m^2 = qm$ for some integer $m$.

exact.text: Show that for any pair of natural numbers $(x, y)$, if there exists an integer $k$ such that $2x^2 = ky$, then the sum $x^2 + y$ cannot be expressed as $m^2$ for any $m \in \mathbb{Z}$.

paraphrase.text: Suppose $a$ and $b$ are positive integers. Show that if there exists an integer $c$ such that $c^2 = a^2 + b$, then $b$ does not divide $2a^2$.

style.text: Suppose $a$ and $b$ are natural numbers. If there exists an integer $k$ such that $2a^2 = kb$, show that $a^2 + b$ can never be the square of an integer.

exact.text: Let $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n \in \{0, 1\}$ be labels assigned to the vertices of a convex $n$-gon in cyclic order. Show that there exists a triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ of the $n$-gon such that the set of values $S = \{x_i + x_j + x_k : \Delta v_i v_j v_k \in \mathcal{T}\}$ is a subset of $\{m, m+1\}$ for some $m \in \{0, 1, 2\}$.

paraphrase.text: Let $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \{0, 1\}$ be labels on the vertices of a convex $n$-gon. Show that there exists a triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ of the $n$-gon such that for any two triangles $T_1, T_2 \in \mathcal{T}$, the sums of labels of their respective vertices, $S(T_1)$ and $S(T_2)$, satisfy $|S(T_1) - S(T_2)| \le 1$.

style.text: A binary string $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ is arranged in a circle. A triangulation of the $n$-gon with these values at its vertices is created by choosing $n-3$ non-crossing diagonals. For each triangle, let $S$ be the sum of the values at its three vertices. Show that there exists a triangulation such that $\max(S) - \min(S) \le 1$.

exact.text: Consider the sequence $s_n = x^n + y^n$ for $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. \\ i) Show that if $s_1, s_2, s_4 \in \mathbb{Z}$, then $s_n \in \mathbb{Z}$ for every $n \in \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$. \\ ii) Provide a pair $(x, y) \in (\mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Z})^2$ satisfying $s_1, s_2, s_4 \in \mathbb{Z}$. \\ iii) Identify $(x, y) \in (\mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Z})^2$ such that $s_1, s_2, s_3 \in \mathbb{Z}$ but $s_4 \notin \mathbb{Z}$.

paraphrase.text: Given $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ where $x+y \in \mathbb{Z}$, $x^2+y^2 \in \mathbb{Z}$, and $x^4+y^4 \in \mathbb{Z}$, show that $x^n+y^n \in \mathbb{Z}$ for every positive integer $n$. Additionally, provide non-integer pairs $(x,y)$ satisfying these conditions, and show that if $x^4+y^4$ is replaced by $x^3+y^3$ in the premise, $x^4+y^4$ need not be an integer.

style.text:
Consider a quadratic equation $t^2 - St + P = 0$ with real roots $\alpha$ and $ eta$. Suppose that $S$, $\alpha^2 +  eta^2$, and $\alpha^4 +  eta^4$ are all elements of $\mathbb{Z}$. 

i) Show that $\alpha^k +  eta^k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for every positive integer $k$. 
ii) Provide non-integers $\alpha,  eta$ satisfying these conditions. 
iii) Provide non-integers $\alpha,  eta$ such that $S$, $\alpha^2 +  eta^2$, and $\alpha^3 +  eta^3$ are integers, but $\alpha^4 +  eta^4 
otin \mathbb{Z}$.

exact.text: Let $f(x) = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$. Demonstrate that the equation $f(x^2) + f(x) = 1$ has no solutions in $\mathbb{Q}$, but provide a value $x \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}$ for which the identity holds.

paraphrase.text: Show that the equation $x^2 + x = \lfloor x^2 \rfloor + \lfloor x \rfloor + 1$ has no solutions in $\mathbb{Q}$, and provide a specific $x \in \mathbb{R}$ that solves it.

style.text: Let $f(t) = \{t^2\} + \{t\}$. Show that $1$ is not in the image of $f$ when restricted to the domain $\mathbb{Q}$, but that there exists $t \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}$ such that $f(t) = 1$.

exact.text: Given positive reals $x_1, \dots, x_n$ with $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i = S$, show that $$\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{x_i^3}{x_i^2 + x_{i+1}x_{i+2}} \ge \frac{S}{2}$$ where indices are taken modulo $n$.

paraphrase.text: Given $n$ positive variables $x_k$ satisfying $x_1 + x_2 + \dots + x_n = 1$, establish the lower bound $\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{x_k^2}{x_k + \frac{x_{k+1}x_{k+2}}{x_k}} \ge \frac{1}{2}$, where $x_{n+1} = x_1$ and $x_{n+2} = x_2$.

style.text: Given a sequence of positive reals $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ with a sum of $S$, show that $\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{x_k^3}{x_k^2 + x_{k+1}x_{k+2}} \ge \frac{S}{2}$, where $x_{n+1}=x_1$ and $x_{n+2}=x_2$.

exact.text: Let $\mathcal{A} = \{A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N\}$ and $\mathcal{B} = \{B_1, B_2, \dots, B_{N+K}\}$ be two partitions of a finite set $S$ into non-empty subsets. For any $s \in S$, let $\sigma_{\mathcal{A}}(s)$ and $\sigma_{\mathcal{B}}(s)$ denote the cardinality of the subset containing $s$ in the respective partitions. Show that the set $S_{<} = \{s \in S : \sigma_{\mathcal{B}}(s) < \sigma_{\mathcal{A}}(s)\}$ satisfies $|S_{<}| \ge K+1$.

paraphrase.text: Let $X$ be a finite set, and let $\mathcal{A} = \{A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N\}$ and $\mathcal{B} = \{B_1, B_2, \dots, B_{N+K}\}$ be two partitions of $X$ into non-empty subsets. For any $x \in X$, let $\sigma_{\mathcal{A}}(x)$ and $\sigma_{\mathcal{B}}(x)$ denote the cardinality of the subset in $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$, respectively, that contains $x$. Show that the cardinality of the set $\{x \in X : \sigma_{\mathcal{B}}(x) < \sigma_{\mathcal{A}}(x)\}$ is at least $K+1$.

style.text: A collection of $m$ items is partitioned into $x$ disjoint non-empty sets $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_x$. The same $m$ items are then partitioned into $x+y$ disjoint non-empty sets $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_{x+y}$, where $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. Let $s(p)$ denote the size of the set containing item $p$ in a partition. Show that there are at least $y+1$ items $p$ such that $s_B(p) < s_A(p)$.

exact.text: Consider a polyomino $P$ embedded in a $\mathbb{Z}^2$ checkerboard tiling where each cell $c$ is assigned a parity $\sigma(c) \in \{-1, 1\}$. Let $S = \sum_{c \in P} \sigma(c)$ denote the net color balance of the squares. If $E$ is the set of unit segments forming the boundary $\partial P$, and each $e \in E$ inherits the parity $\sigma(c)$ of the unique square $c \in P$ incident to it, prove that $\sum_{e \in E} \sigma(e) = 4S$.

paraphrase.text: Consider a lattice polygon $P$ formed by the union of $n$ unit squares in a standard checkerboard tiling. Let $n_1$ and $n_2$ denote the counts of black and white squares within $P$, respectively. If the perimeter of $P$ consists of $e_1$ segments bordering black squares and $e_2$ segments bordering white squares, show that $e_1 - e_2 = 4(n_1 - n_2)$.

style.text: A polyomino is formed on a checkered lattice. Let $n_1$ be the number of dark unit cells and $n_2$ be the number of light unit cells contained in the polyomino. Let $e_1$ be the number of unit segments on the boundary of the polyomino that belong to a dark cell, and $e_2$ be the number of unit segments on the boundary that belong to a light cell. Show that $e_1 - e_2 = 4(n_1 - n_2)$.

exact.text: Find the set of all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ for which the product of the first $n$ even integers is strictly less than the product of the first $n$ odd integers starting from $n+1$, specifically: $\prod_{k=1}^n (2k) < \prod_{k=1}^n (n+k)$.

paraphrase.text: Find all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ satisfying the inequality $\prod_{k=1}^n k < \prod_{k=1}^n (2k-1)$.

style.text: Find the set of all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ for which the inequality $\frac{(2n)!}{2^n (n!)^2} > 1$ holds.

exact.text: A convex $n$-gon is constructed such that the number of its exterior angles measuring less than $90^\circ$ is exactly 3. Find the maximum possible value of $n$.

paraphrase.text: A convex $n$-gon is constructed such that the number of its exterior angles measuring less than $90^\circ$ is exactly three. Determine the maximum possible value of $n$.

style.text: In a convex $n$-gon, let $S$ be the set of its exterior angles. If $|\{e \in S : e < 90^\circ\}| = 3$, determine the maximum possible value of $n$.

exact.text: Let $d(n)$ denote the number of positive divisors of $n$. Determine which value is greater: $d((3 \cdot 11 \cdot 61)^2)$ or $d(2^{12} \cdot 5)$.

paraphrase.text: Let $\tau(n)$ denote the number of positive divisors of $n$. Determine which value is greater: $\tau((3 \cdot 11 \cdot 61)^2)$ or $\tau(2^{12} \cdot 5)$.

style.text: Let $a = 33^2 \cdot 61^2$ and $b = 2^{12} \cdot 5$. Determine which of these two integers possesses a greater number of positive factors.

exact.text: Show that there exist no integers $x$ and $y$ satisfying the equality $$3(x^2+4)^2 + 1965 = (5y)^2.$$

paraphrase.text: Show that the Diophantine equation $3(x^2+4)^2 + 1965 = (5y)^2$ has no solutions in the set of integers $\mathbb{Z}$.

style.text: Determine all pairs of integers $(m, n)$ such that $3(m^2+4)^2 + 1965 = (5n)^2$.

exact.text: Find the set of all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ for which the equation $2^k - 3^n = 7$ has a solution in the positive integers $k$.

paraphrase.text: Find the set of all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ for which there exists an integer $k$ such that the equality $2^k - 3^n = 7$ holds.

style.text: Find the set of all $k \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ for which there exists an integer $m$ satisfying the equation $3^k = 2^m - 7$.

exact.text: Let $S = \{1, 2, \dots, 200\} \times \{1, 2, \dots, 100\} \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$. Determine the cardinality of the set $\{\{P, Q\} : P, Q \in S, \|P-Q\|^2 = 5\}$.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \{1, 2, \dots, 200\} \times \{1, 2, \dots, 100\}$. Determine the number of subsets $\{P, Q\} \subseteq S$ such that the Euclidean distance $d(P, Q)$ satisfies $d(P, Q)^2 = 5$.

style.text: In a $200 \times 100$ rectangular grid of pins, a rubber band is stretched between two pins to form a segment of length $\sqrt{5}$. How many distinct pairs of pins can be chosen to form such a segment?

exact.text: For any three real numbers $x, y, z$ such that $x \ge y \ge z$, demonstrate that the inequality $x^2 - y^2 + z^2 - (x - y + z)^2 \ge 0$ holds.

paraphrase.text: For any three real numbers $x, y, z$ such that $x \le y \le z$, show that the inequality $y^2 - x^2 \le z^2 - (z - y + x)^2$ holds.

style.text: Given a set of three real numbers $\{x, y, z\}$, let $m$ be the median value and $M, \mu$ be the maximum and minimum values respectively. Show that $M^2 + \mu^2 - m^2 \ge (M + \mu - m)^2$.

exact.text: Let the sequence $\{a_k\}_{k=1}^n$ be defined by $a_1 = 1$ and $a_k = \sqrt{k + a_{k-1}}$ for $k = 2, 3, \dots, n$. Show that $a_n < \sqrt{n} + 1$ holds for any $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$.

paraphrase.text: Let a sequence of real numbers be defined by $x_1 = 1$ and $x_k = \sqrt{k + x_{k-1}}$ for $k = 2, 3, \dots, n$. Show that for any $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, the inequality $x_n - \sqrt{n} < 1$ holds.

style.text: Define a sequence by $a_1 = 1$ and $a_k = \sqrt{k + a_{k-1}}$ for $k > 1$. Show that $a_n - \sqrt{n} < 1$ holds for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$.

exact.text: Consider a sequence of $50$ terms $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{50}$ arranged in a circle, where each $a_i \in \{1, 2\}$. It is given that $a_i = a_{i+1} = a_{i+2}$ is impossible for all $i$ (with indices taken modulo $50$). If the value $2$ appears exactly $30$ times and the value $1$ appears exactly $20$ times, show that the sum $S = \sum_{i=1}^{50} a_i a_{i+1} a_{i+2}$ is invariant across all such configurations and find its value.

paraphrase.text: Consider a sequence $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{50}$ with $x_i \in \{1, 2\}$ such that $x_i = x_{i+50}$ for all $i$ and no three indices in cyclic succession satisfy $x_i = x_{i+1} = x_{i+2}$. If the value $1$ appears exactly $20$ times in the sequence, evaluate the cyclic sum $\sum_{k=1}^{50} x_k x_{k+1} x_{k+2}$.

style.text: A sequence $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{50}$ with $x_i \in \{1, 2\}$ and $x_{n+50} = x_n$ contains exactly twenty $1$s and thirty $2$s. It is known that $x_i = x_{i+1} = x_{i+2}$ is impossible for any $i$. Evaluate $\sum_{k=1}^{50} x_{k-1}x_k x_{k+1}$.

exact.text: Let $S = \{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2014}\}$ be a multiset such that $S \subset \{-1, 0, 1\}$. Determine the minimum value of $\frac{1}{2} \left[ \left( \sum_{k=1}^{2014} x_k \right)^2 - \sum_{k=1}^{2014} x_k^2 \right]$.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i$ and $Q = \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i^2$, where $n = 2014$ and $a_i \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$. Determine the minimum value of $\frac{1}{2}(S^2 - Q)$.

style.text: Let $S$ be a set of $2014$ integers where each element $s \in S$ satisfies $s^3 = s$. Determine the minimum possible value of $(\sum_{s \in S} s)^2 - \sum_{s \in S} s^2$.

exact.text: Consider a sequence of bits $b_0, b_1, \dots, b_{11}$ arranged in a circle, initially set to $(1, 0, 0, \dots, 0)$. A move consists of choosing an index $i$ and replacing $b_j$ with $1-b_j$ for all $j \in \{i, i+1, \dots, i+5\} \pmod{12}$. Show that the state where $b_1 = 1$ and all other $b_j = 0$ is unreachable.

paraphrase.text: Consider a sequence $x_n \in \{0, 1\}$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{12}$ where indices are taken modulo 12. Initially, $x_0 = 1$ and $x_n = 0$ for $n \in \{1, \dots, 11\}$. An operation consists of adding $1$ to $x_i, x_{i+1}, \dots, x_{i+5}$ modulo 2 for some $i$. Show that the state $x_1 = 1$ and $x_n = 0$ for $n \in \{0, 2, 3, \dots, 11\}$ is unreachable.

style.text: A circular array of 12 light bulbs is controlled by a switchboard. Initially, bulb $L_1$ is OFF and all others are ON. A single operation consists of toggling the state (ON to OFF, or OFF to ON) of exactly six adjacent bulbs. Is it possible to reach a state where bulb $L_2$ is OFF and all other bulbs are ON?

exact.text: In triangle $PQR$, the interior angles at vertices $P$ and $Q$ satisfy $\tan P = 1$ and $\tan Q = 2$. Evaluate the side length ratio $\frac{QR}{PQ}$ using the Law of Sines.

paraphrase.text: In triangle $PQR$, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the internal angles at vertices $P$ and $Q$ respectively. If $\alpha = \frac{\pi}{4}$ and $\beta = \arctan(2)$, find the value of $\frac{\sin \alpha}{\sin(\pi - \alpha - \beta)}$.

style.text: In $\triangle PQR$, the altitudes from $Q$ and $R$ intersect at $H$. If the slope of $PQ$ is $2$ and the slope of $PR$ is $1$ in a coordinate system where $QR$ lies on the $x$-axis, find the value of $\frac{\sin \angle RPQ}{\sin \angle PRQ}$.

exact.text: For a fixed positive integer $n$, define $f(k)$ to be the unique odd integer such that $k = 2^j f(k)$ for some non-negative integer $j$. Evaluate $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} f(n+i)$.

paraphrase.text: For a fixed positive integer $m$, let $v_2(k)$ denote the largest integer $v$ such that $2^v$ divides $k$. Evaluate the sum $\sum_{k=m}^{2m-1} \frac{k}{2^{v_2(k)}}$.

style.text: For a fixed positive integer $k$, let $f(m)$ denote the value $m \cdot 2^{-v_2(m)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the highest power of $2$ dividing $m$. Calculate the value of $\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} f(k+j)$.

exact.text: Suppose $p, q, r, s$ are distinct real numbers satisfying the following system of equations: $p+q = 10r$, $pq = -11s$, $r+s = 10p$, and $rs = -11q$. Calculate the value of $p+q+r+s$.

paraphrase.text: Suppose $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4 \in \mathbb{R}$ are distinct. If the roots of $t^2 - 10x_3 t = 11x_4$ are $t=x_1$ and $t=x_2$, while the roots of $t^2 - 10x_1 t = 11x_2$ are $t=x_3$ and $t=x_4$, find the value of $\sum_{i=1}^4 x_i$.

style.text: Four distinct values $p, q, r, s$ satisfy the following conditions: $p$ and $q$ are the roots of $z^2 - 10r z = 11s$, while $r$ and $s$ are the roots of $z^2 - 10p z = 11q$. Find the value of $p + q + r + s$.

exact.text: Let $S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$. A sequence of distinct elements is chosen from $S$ by selecting one element at a time uniformly at random without replacement. The process terminates as soon as a special marker, which is equally likely to appear before the first element, after any element, or after the last element of a random permutation of $S \cup \{\text{marker}\}$, is encountered. Determine the probability that the sum of the elements selected before the marker is at least $10$.

paraphrase.text: Consider a set of six cards: one labeled 'STOP' and the others labeled with the integers $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$. If the cards are arranged in a random permutation $\sigma = (c_1, c_2, \dots, c_6)$, let $k$ be the index such that $c_k = \text{'STOP'}$. Find the probability that $\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} c_i \ge 10$.

style.text: A deck contains 6 cards: an 'End' card and five numbered cards $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$. A player deals cards from the shuffled deck one by one. The game terminates immediately when the 'End' card is dealt. What is the probability that the sum of the values on the cards dealt (excluding the 'End' card) is greater than or equal to $10$?

exact.text: In a quadrilateral $ABCD$, given the side lengths $a=6$, $b=9$, $c=18$, and $d=5$ (where $a, b, c, d$ are the lengths of sides $AB, BC, CD, DA$ respectively), find the value of $k \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that a triangle with sides $a, b, k$ and a triangle with sides $c, d, k$ both satisfy the triangle inequality.

paraphrase.text: In a plane, two triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$ are joined along a common edge $AC$. If the lengths of the remaining sides are $AB=6$, $BC=9$, $CD=18$, and $DA=5$, find the unique integer $k$ such that $|AC|=k$.

style.text: In a convex polygon $PQRS$, the side lengths are $PQ=5$, $QR=18$, $RS=9$, and $SP=6$. If the length of the segment $QS$ is an integer, find its value.

exact.text: Let $z = x + iy$ with $y \neq 0$. Find the set of all such $z \in \mathbb{C}$ that minimize the expression $1 + 5\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)^4 - 10\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)^2$.

paraphrase.text: Find the set of all $z = x + iy \in \mathbb{C}$ with $y \neq 0$ that minimize the expression $\frac{\text{Im}(z^5)}{(\text{Im} z)^5}$.

style.text: Find all $w = a + bi \in \mathbb{C}$ with $b \neq 0$ that minimize the value of the expression $\frac{\text{Im}(w^5)}{(\text{Im}(w))^5}$.

exact.text: A $k \times k \times k$ lattice of unit cells (where $k=8$) has its faces colored such that three faces meeting at a vertex are white and the remaining three faces are red. Given that this configuration ensures every corner cell has both colors present, determine the number of unit cells situated on the boundary that possess both a white and a red face.

paraphrase.text: A large cube is assembled from $n^3$ unit blocks, where $n=8$. Three faces of the large cube are colored white and the remaining three are colored red. It is observed that every corner block possesses faces of both colors. Determine the total number of unit blocks that have at least one face of each color.

style.text: A $10 \times 10 \times 10$ block of marble is composed of unit $1 \times 1 \times 1$ cubes. Three faces of the block are polished, and the remaining three are left rough. It is observed that every corner unit cube has at least one polished face and at least one rough face. How many unit cubes in the block possess both a polished face and a rough face?

exact.text: The values $a$ and $b$ are the non-equal roots of the system of equations $a - (b-2)^2 + 4 = 0$ and $b - (a-2)^2 + 4 = 0$. Calculate the sum of the squares of these values.

paraphrase.text: Suppose $a$ and $b$ are two different real values satisfying the system of equations $a + 4 = b^2 - 4b + 4$ and $b + 4 = a^2 - 4a + 4$. Find the value of $a^2 + b^2$.

style.text: Two different values $a$ and $b$ satisfy the system of equations $a = b^2 - 4b$ and $b = a^2 - 4a$. Find the value of $a^2 + b^2$.

exact.text: Determine all pairs of rational numbers $(x, y)$ satisfying the equation $\sin^2\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right) = x + \sqrt{y}$.

paraphrase.text: Determine all pairs of rational numbers $(x, y)$ satisfying the equation $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4}\sin(150^\circ) = x + \sqrt{y}$.

style.text: Determine the pair of rational numbers $(x, y)$ that satisfy the equation $\cos^2 \frac{\pi}{12} = x + \sqrt{y}$.

exact.text: Let $S$ be the set of vectors $\mathbf{v} = (x, y, z, w) \in \mathbb{R}^4$ satisfying the equation $\|\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{c}\|^2 = R^2$ where $\mathbf{c} = (\frac{1}{2}, \frac{3}{2}, \frac{5}{2}, \frac{7}{2})$ and $R^2 = 4 + \frac{1^2+3^2+5^2+7^2}{4}$. Find the maximum value of the dot product $\mathbf{v} \cdot (1, 1, 1, 1)$.

paraphrase.text: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 \in \mathbb{R}$. Given the constraint $\sum_{k=1}^4 (a_k^2 + (2k-1)a_k) = 4$, find the maximum value of $\sum_{k=1}^4 a_k$.

style.text: Find the maximum value of the sum of the coordinates of a point $(a, b, c, d)$ lying on the hypersphere defined by the equation $(a + 1/2)^2 + (b + 3/2)^2 + (c + 5/2)^2 + (d + 7/2)^2 = 25$.

exact.text: In the Cartesian plane, let a circle be defined by $x^2 + y^2 = 1$. A square $\mathcal{Q}$ has two adjacent vertices lying on the circle, while the line containing the opposite side passes through the origin $(0,0)$. Determine the side length $s$ of $\mathcal{Q}$.

paraphrase.text: In the Cartesian plane, a square $PQRS$ with side length $L$ is oriented such that the segment $RS$ lies on the $x$-axis and contains the origin $O(0,0)$. If the vertices $P$ and $Q$ both lie on the unit circle $x^2 + y^2 = 1$, determine the value of $L$.

style.text: In a coordinate plane, a square $PQRS$ has its base $RS$ lying on the $x$-axis such that the origin $O$ is the midpoint of $RS$. If the vertices $P$ and $Q$ lie on the unit circle $x^2 + y^2 = 1$, determine the side length of the square.

exact.text: In a simple graph $G$ with 7 vertices, the degree sequence is $(2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1)$. If an edge is selected uniformly at random from the set of all possible edges in the complete graph $K_7$, what is the probability that this edge is not present in $G$?

paraphrase.text: A simple graph $G$ contains $7$ vertices. The degree sequence of $G$ is $(2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1)$. If a pair of distinct vertices is chosen uniformly at random, what is the probability that there is no edge between them?

style.text: A simple graph $G$ has $7$ vertices. Four vertices have degree $1$ and three vertices have degree $2$. If an edge is selected at random from the set of all possible edges in the complete graph $K_7$, what is the probability that the selected edge is not in $G$?

exact.text: Let $\mathcal{I}_n = [2^n, 2^{n+1}) \cap \mathbb{Z}^+$ for $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. Show that there exists a partition of the set of indices $\mathbb{N}_0$ into three sets $S_1, S_2, S_3$ such that for any $j \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, the equation $x+y=z^2$ has no solutions with $x \in \mathcal{I}_a, y \in \mathcal{I}_b, z \in \mathcal{I}_k$ and $a, b, k \in S_j$, unless $x=y=z=2$.

paraphrase.text: Define a coloring $\chi: \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1, 2\}$ such that $\chi(x) = \chi(y)$ whenever $\lfloor \log_2 x \rfloor = \lfloor \log_2 y \rfloor$. Show that there exists such a coloring where the equation $x+y=z^2$ has no solutions in $\mathbb{N}$ with $\chi(x)=\chi(y)=\chi(z)$, excluding the trivial case $x=y=z=2$.

style.text: Let $f: \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1, 2\}$ be a function. Show that there exists such a function satisfying: (a) $f(x) = f(y)$ whenever $\lfloor \log_2 x \rfloor = \lfloor \log_2 y \rfloor$; (b) if $x, y, z \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(x) = f(y) = f(z)$ and $x+y=z^2$, then $x=y=z=2$.

exact.text: Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}^+$ with the property that for every pair of positive integers $m$ and $n$, the congruence $mf(m) + nf(n) \equiv 0 \pmod{f(m) + f(n) - mn}$ holds.

paraphrase.text: Determine all functions $g: \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}^+$ satisfying the property that for every pair of positive integers $x, y$, the sum $x g(x) + y g(y)$ is a multiple of $g(x) + g(y) - xy$.

style.text: Determine all functions $g: \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}^+$ with the property that for every pair of positive integers $m$ and $n$, the value $mg(m) + ng(n)$ is a multiple of $g(m) + g(n) - mn$.

exact.text: Find every set of primes $\{x, y\}$ such that the sum $x^{y-1} + y^{x-1}$ belongs to the set $\{k^2 : k \in \mathbb{Z}^+\}$.

paraphrase.text: Find all primes $x$ and $y$ such that there exists an integer $k$ satisfying $x^{y-1} + y^{x-1} = k^2$.

style.text: Let $S$ be the set of all pairs of primes $(x, y)$ such that the sum $x^{y-1} + y^{x-1}$ is the square of some integer $k$. Find all elements in $S$.

exact.text: Given a real constant $c \ge n = 2018$, consider $n$ multisets of real numbers $\mathcal{M}_1, \dots, \mathcal{M}_n$ such that every element $x \in \mathcal{M}_i$ is an integer power of $c$. If the sum of elements in each multiset is equal to a fixed value $W$, find the minimum possible value of $\max_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \sum_{i=1}^n \text{count}(c^k, \mathcal{M}_i)$, where $\text{count}(y, \mathcal{M})$ is the multiplicity of $y$ in $\mathcal{M}$.

paraphrase.text: Given an integer $n = 2018$ and a real constant $\lambda \ge n$, consider $n$ collections of objects. Each object has a mass in the set $\{\lambda^j : j \in \mathbb{Z}\}$. Suppose the sum of masses in each collection is equal to a fixed value $S$. If $f(j)$ represents the total number of objects of mass $\lambda^j$ across all $n$ collections, find the minimum possible value of $\max_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} f(j)$.

style.text: A collection of $N=2024$ distinct jars each contains a set of weights. Each weight is a power of $x$, where $x \ge 2024$ is a fixed constant. If every jar has the same total mass $M$, and $f(p)$ denotes the total number of times the weight $x^p$ appears across all jars combined, find the minimum possible value of $\max_{p \in \mathbb{Z}} f(p)$.

exact.text: A set of tokens contains 3 distinct vowels and 6 distinct consonants. Determine the number of permutations of these 9 tokens such that the relative order of the vowels matches their natural alphabetical sequence, and similarly, the relative order of the consonants matches their natural alphabetical sequence.

paraphrase.text: Consider the set of the first nine letters of the alphabet $\{A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I\}$. Calculate the number of permutations where the relative order of the elements in the subset of vowels $V = \{A, E, I\}$ is $(A, E, I)$ and the relative order of the elements in the subset of consonants $C = \{B, C, D, F, G, H\}$ is $(B, C, D, F, G, H)$.

style.text: A string of length $9$ contains $6$ distinct consonants and $3$ distinct vowels. How many such strings can be formed if the relative order of the consonants must be alphabetical, and the relative order of the vowels must also be alphabetical?

exact.text: A right pyramid with a square base has a base perimeter of $48$. If the distance from the apex to the center of the base is $8$, determine the total area of all its faces, including the base.

paraphrase.text: A regular quadrangular pyramid has a base perimeter of $48$ and an altitude of $8$. Determine the total area of its five faces.

style.text: In the Cartesian coordinate system, a pyramid has a square base with vertices at $(\pm 6, \pm 6, 0)$. The apex of the pyramid is located at the point $(0, 0, 8)$. Calculate the total surface area of this solid.

exact.text: Determine all pairs of positive integers $(x, y)$ such that the expression $\frac{(3^x-1)(3^x+2)}{2}$ is a power of some prime $q$ with exponent $y$.

paraphrase.text: Determine all couples $(a, b) \in \mathbb{Z}^+ \times \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that the expression $\frac{1}{2}(3^a - 1)(3^a + 2)$ is equal to the $b$-th power of some prime $q$.

style.text: Determine all ordered pairs of positive integers $(a, b)$ such that the equation $(3^a-1)(3^a+2) = 2p^b$ holds for some prime $p$.

exact.text: Let $T = (V, E)$ be a tournament graph on $n$ vertices. Show that there is a vertex $v \in V$ such that for every $u \in V \setminus \{v\}$, the distance $d(v, u)$ satisfies $1 \le d(v, u) \le 2$.

paraphrase.text: In a round-robin tournament with $n$ players where every match results in a win or a loss, show that there exists a player $P$ such that for every other player $Q$, either $P$ beat $Q$ or $P$ beat some player $R$ who beat $Q$.

style.text: In a round-robin tournament with $n$ players, where no matches end in a draw, show that there is at least one player $P$ such that for every other player $Q$, either $P$ defeated $Q$, or $P$ defeated someone who defeated $Q$.

exact.text:
Let $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_{299} \in \mathbb{Z}$ be arranged in a circle, initially $(1, 0, 0, \dots, 0)$. Two operations are permitted: 
1. Replace the vector $\mathbf{x}$ with $M\mathbf{x}$, where $M$ is the circulant matrix with diagonal 1 and sub/super-diagonals $-1$.
2. For any $i$, replace $(x_i, x_{i+3 \pmod{300}})$ with $(x_i \pm 1, x_{i+3 \pmod{300}} \pm 1)$.
Determine if it is possible to reach a state containing:\na) exactly two adjacent 1s and 298 zeros.\nb) exactly three adjacent 1s and 297 zeros.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \sum_{i=0}^{299} a_i z^i \in \mathbb{Z}[z]/(z^{300}-1)$ represent a configuration of numbers on a circle. Two operations are allowed: (i) $S \mapsto S \cdot (1 - z - z^{-1})$ and (ii) $S \mapsto S \pm (z^k + z^{k+3})$ for any $k \in \{0, \dots, 299\}$. Starting from $S = 1$, can we reach (a) $1+z$ or (b) $1+z+z^2$?

style.text: Let $S = \{a_0, a_1, \dots, a_{299}\}$ be a sequence of integers arranged in a ring, initially $a_0 = 1$ and $a_k = 0$ for $k \neq 0$. You can perform two operations: (i) replace the state vector $\mathbf{a}$ with $(I - M - M^{-1})\mathbf{a}$ where $M$ is the cyclic shift operator, or (ii) add an integer $d$ to both $a_k$ and $a_{k+3 \pmod{300}}$ for any $k$. Determine if it is possible to reach a state where: (a) $a_0=a_1=1$ and all other $a_i=0$. (b) $a_0=a_1=a_2=1$ and all other $a_i=0$.

exact.text: Prove that the field extension $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2})$ is a field by showing that every non-zero element $\alpha = a + b \sqrt[3]{2} + c \sqrt[3]{4}$ with $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q}$ possesses a multiplicative inverse in the form $d + e \sqrt[3]{2} + f \sqrt[3]{4}$ for some $d, e, f \in \mathbb{Q}$.

paraphrase.text: Prove that every non-zero element of the set $\{ a + b \sqrt[3]{2} + c \sqrt[3]{4} : a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q} \}$ has a multiplicative inverse within the same set.

style.text: Let $\alpha = \sqrt[3]{2}$. Prove that for any $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q}$ not all zero, the reciprocal of $a + b\alpha + c\alpha^2$ can be expressed in the form $p + q\alpha + r\alpha^2$ where $p, q, r$ are rational numbers.

exact.text: Define a relation $\mathcal{R} \subset \mathbb{N}_0 \times \mathbb{N}_0$ such that $x \mathcal{R} y$ if and only if the decimal sum $x+y$ belongs to the set $\{ \sum_{i=0}^k d_i 10^i : d_i \in \{0, 1\} \}$. Let $A$ and $B$ be infinite subsets of $\mathbb{N}_0$ satisfying $B = \{ y \in \mathbb{N}_0 : \forall a \in A, a \mathcal{R} y \}$ and $A = \{ x \in \mathbb{N}_0 : \forall b \in B, x \mathcal{R} b \}$. Prove that there exists $S \in \{A, B\}$ such that the set $\{ n \in \mathbb{N}_0 : n \in S \text{ and } n+1 \in S \}$ is infinite.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \{ n \in \mathbb{N}_0 : n = \sum_{i=0}^k d_i 10^i, d_i \in \{0, 1\} \}$.
